\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{कीलः} (kīlaḥ)}{कीलः (kīlaḥ)}]{\sk{कीलः} (kīlaḥ) — a nail (to hammer)}

\label{lesson:SA-C100-kilah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a curtain, then the Sanskrit for a lock.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{कीलः}}
\textbf{\sk{कीलः}} — \emph{kīlaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a nail (to hammer)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kīla} \textquotedblleft{}a stake, a peg, a pin\textquotedblright{} has no settled origin: CDIAL 3202 notes an Indo-European account (EWA) but also a proposal of non-Aryan origin, since forms with \emph{kh-} stand beside it. It lives on as Hindi \emph{kīl} \textquotedblleft{}nail\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3202).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for a curtain, then the Sanskrit for a lock, then say \emph{kīlaḥ} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{मुद्गरः} (mudgaraḥ)}{मुद्गरः (mudgaraḥ)}]{\sk{मुद्गरः} (mudgaraḥ) — a hammer}

\label{lesson:SA-C100-mudgarah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a lock, then the Sanskrit for a nail.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{मुद्गरः}}
\textbf{\sk{मुद्गरः}} — \emph{mudgaraḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a hammer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
MW takes \emph{mudgara} \textquotedblleft{}a hammer, a mallet\textquotedblright{} as probably formed from \emph{mudga} \textquotedblleft{}mung bean\textquotedblright{}, but gives no further account, so its source is uncertain. It lives on as Marathi and Gujarati \emph{mogar} \textquotedblleft{}mallet\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10199).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{कर्तरी} (kartarī)}{कर्तरी (kartarī)}]{\sk{कर्तरी} (kartarī) — scissors}

\label{lesson:SA-C100-kartari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a nail, then the Sanskrit for a hammer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{कर्तरी}}
\textbf{\sk{कर्तरी}} — \emph{kartarī} — \textquotedblleft{}scissors\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kartarī} \textquotedblleft{}scissors\textquotedblright{} comes from the root √kṛt \textquotedblleft{}cut\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2858), which MW compares with Latin \emph{curtus} \textquotedblleft{}cut short\textquotedblright{}, the source of English \emph{curt}. It lives on as Hindi and Punjabi \emph{katarnī} \textquotedblleft{}scissors\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2858).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{सूचिः} (sūciḥ)}{सूचिः (sūciḥ)}]{\sk{सूचिः} (sūciḥ) — a needle}

\label{lesson:SA-C100-sucih}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a hammer, then the Sanskrit for scissors.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{सूचिः}}
\textbf{\sk{सूचिः}} — \emph{sūciḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a needle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
MW connects \emph{sūci} \textquotedblleft{}needle\textquotedblright{} with \emph{sūtra} \textquotedblleft{}thread\textquotedblright{} and the root √siv \textquotedblleft{}sew\textquotedblright{}, though CDIAL 13551 notes that some forms point to an older \emph{śūci-}, so the link is not settled. It lives on as Hindi \emph{sūī} and Bengali \emph{sui} \textquotedblleft{}needle\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13551).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{सूत्रम्} (sūtram)}{सूत्रम् (sūtram)}]{\sk{सूत्रम्} (sūtram) — thread}

\label{lesson:SA-C100-sutram}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for scissors, then the Sanskrit for a needle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{सूत्रम्}}
\textbf{\sk{सूत्रम्}} — \emph{sūtram} — \textquotedblleft{}thread\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sūtra} \textquotedblleft{}thread\textquotedblright{} comes from the root √siv \textquotedblleft{}sew\textquotedblright{} (MW), an Indo-European root (EtymDB) that also gave English \emph{sew} and Latin \emph{suere}. It lives on as Hindi \emph{sūt} \textquotedblleft{}thread\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13561), and a \emph{sūtra} of rules is a \textquotedblleft{}thread\textquotedblright{} of short lines.
\end{cousinweb}
